vignette: Sara, a 69-year-old Middle Eastern woman and fast food worker, has been haunted by the memories of a traumatic stalking incident that occurred over two years ago. Her husband, Nader, often notices her anxiety when she recounts details of the event. Sara vividly remembers the night when she was first approached by a man in the parking lot outside work. He began following her home and leaving notes on her car, with his presence becoming increasingly menacing as time went on. The incident occurred in a particularly smoky area near her workplace, and to this day, whenever she catches a whiff of cigarette smoke or motor oil, it triggers vivid flashbacks that make her feel as if the event is happening all over again. Her husband has noticed her behavior change dramatically after these episodes; sometimes she can recall the details of what happened but feels completely numb, as though the experience did not happen to her at all. Since the stalking began, Sara has become increasingly vigilant and anxious. She wakes up multiple times each night to check whether her home is secure, ensuring that every door and window is locked. Even during the day, she constantly studies people's faces and body language in an attempt to detect any potential threats. Her fear is heightened whenever she sees anyone who resembles the stalker, which often causes her to avoid going out alone. Sara's occupation as a fast food worker has also been affected by these symptoms. She avoids certain areas of the restaurant where she feels more vulnerable and frequently checks that the doors leading outside are locked. This constant state of alertness has made it difficult for her to focus on her work, leading to increased stress at her job. Sara's relationship with Nader has been strained as well. Her fear and anxiety have led her to become distant from him, both emotionally and physically. She feels like she doesn't know herself anymore and is certain that if she dwells too much on the event, she won't be able to handle it. This thought avoidance has caused a rift between them, with Nader feeling helpless as he watches Sara withdraw into her own world. The stalking experience has also led to a pervasive sense of mistrust towards others. Sara believes people can't be trusted and is constantly on guard around everyone, even those she once considered close friends. Her fear that someone else might harm her or invade her privacy has made it difficult for her to form new connections or maintain existing ones. What finally brought Sara to seek help was an episode where she nearly had a panic attack at work after smelling something reminiscent of the event. She realized that her constant vigilance and avoidance were taking a significant toll on both her personal life and job performance. Despite her fears, she is most hopeful for a way to regain control over her thoughts and emotions so that she can feel safe again in her daily routine. Sara's current state is marked by intense fear and uncertainty about the future. She hopes to find a way to manage her symptoms and rebuild trust in herself and others, reclaiming her sense of identity and peace.
